Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for taking this. We are NebulaAI (CTO here) and evaluating reserved/dedicated capacity for our customer-facing inference tier. Attached is a quarter of anonymized logs (nebula_traffic_sample_q2.csv) — token counts, session ids, prompt vs completion length, and p95 latencies for our current hosted endpoints.

Quick context:
- Peak concurrent active sessions (observed): 1,100
- Typical prompt length: 180 tokens; median completion: 55 tokens
- 60% of requests are short completions (<32 tokens); 10% are long-form (>1024 tokens) during batch jobs
- We expect steady growth +30% q/q for the next 6 months after launch

High-level ask: can you help us map this to a recommended reserved capacity commitment (GPU SKU mix, instance count, burst strategy) and an expected cost-per-1000-tokens estimate? We also need guidance on session affinity and KV cache sizing — our product has multi-turn chat with long context windows.

We can join an intake call this week. Availability: Thu 2pm–4pm PT or Fri 10am–12pm PT.

Thanks,
Emily

Thanks for looping me in. I pulled the CSV and did a quick pass — high level notes below (will walk through on call):

- Observed token mix suggests a bifurcated deployment:
  * Latency-critical user-facing slice (≈60–70% requests, median <100 tokens) — optimize for low p99 and streaming; favor smaller but more numerous GPUs (A10x2-like mix) with prefix KV caching enabled.
  * Heavy/batch long-form slice (≈10–15% long >1024 tokens, plus scheduled jobs) — optimize for throughput and memory; favor fewer beefier GPUs (A100/H100 class) with larger per-instance memory and relaxed latency SLOs.

- Concurrency: your current peak 1,100 concurrent sessions maps to ~0.9k–1.2k active model inference streams depending on session overlap and average token generation rate. For an initial reserved commit we typically recommend sizing to cover 70–80% of forecasted peak traffic and rely on burst capacity for tails.

- KV cache: with multi-turn and long context, plan for ~3–4x working set per active session compared to stateless calls — will need to see the session TTL distribution in the CSV to finalize.

Request for the call: please have a sample of session TTLs and the percentage of sessions using streaming. I've attached our short pre-sales sizer (answers will speed modeling).

Marissa
